phrases.latin: Quot noctēs adhūc dormiēmus, dum avia veniat? — Trēs.
phrases.english: How many sleeps till Grandma comes? — Three.

phrases.latin: Prōvīsam quam mox vir meus redeat domum.
phrases.english: I’ll go and see how soon my husband is coming home.

phrases.latin: spatia omnis temporis nōn numerō diērum sed noctium fīniunt
phrases.english: they measure every span of time by the number not of days but of nights (of the Gauls)

phrases.latin: Nec diērum numerum, ut nōs, sed noctium computant.
phrases.english: They do not count the number of days, as we do, but of nights (of the Germans).

sources: Lewis & Short: mox
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 87, 330.
